kitDescription: Sakura: Bloom in Summer is a Wind AR Burst-III attacker whose damage comes almost entirely from two named effects she maintains on herself and the boss. At the start of the fight she immediately force-casts her Skill 2, which puts 'Dancing Flower' on herself (+15.64% Attack Damage for 15 seconds) and stamps 'Sakura Petals' on the highest-ATK enemy — a sustained damage-over-time that ticks for 256% of her final ATK every second for 15 seconds; Skill 2 then re-fires on its 30-second cooldown, so both effects run in six 15-second windows across a 3-minute fight (about 50% uptime). Her burst hits random enemies ten times in sequence for 457.14% of final ATK each (4571.4% total per cast) and leaves a stacking sustained DoT of 35.16% per second for 10 seconds on those same targets — against a single boss all ten sequential hits land on it, so the DoT opens at its full 10 stacks. Her Skill 1 also carries three riders that only trigger when an ally or she destroys an enemy part: a self Sustained Damage buff and duration extensions to both Dancing Flower and Sakura Petals. On the scope-lock boss, which has no destructible parts, none of those three riders can ever fire, so they contribute nothing to her graded damage.

redAssertions: S1a 'first sustained tick within 2s' — RECON_ERROR: the blind's `sustained` selector filters on e.bucket==='sustained' || e.flavor==='sustained'; damage events carry neither (bucket ∈ normal|skill|burst, no flavor field), so the array is empty for every run. Driver's pin shows the first Sakura Petals tick at sec=1.00 — the assertion's intent is satisfied.

S2a 'Dancing Flower buffApply value ≈ 15.64 exists' — GENUINE DIVERGENCE, documented (⚑3): driver ships 7.82 always-on = 15.64 × 90/180, the SSOT-prescribed time-average for a duration buff carried on a passive at the datamined 30s CD. The blind had no datamine and assumed CD=15 (100% uptime); its own S6 caveat recipes exactly the field the driver holds.

S2a 'zeroing Dancing Flower strictly lowers sakura' — RECON_ERROR: the counterfactual mutates `ov.skill2?.blocks`, but the override file is slot-keyed (`override.skill2` IS the block array; there is no `.blocks`), so the patch is a no-op and totals stay identical. Verifiable directly against §7b.

S2b '256% ticks at 1s spacing' — RECON_ERROR: voided by BOTH the empty `sustained` selector and `nearPct`, which reads `ev.mult` first; `ev.mult` is the multiplier-decomposition OBJECT, so Math.abs(obj − pct) is NaN and nearPct returns false for every event. Correct field is ev.atkPct.
S2b 'Sakura Petals RECURS (>15 ticks, gaps > 1s)' — RECON_ERROR: same two helper bugs. Driver's pin measures 90 ticks in six 30s-spaced bands.
Ba '10 × 457.14 hits per cast' — RECON_ERROR: nearPct bug. Driver's pin finds 60 hits over 6 casts at atkPct 457.14 exactly.

Ba 'volley is FB-exempt and range-exempt' — RECON_ERROR: nearPct bug leaves the volley array empty, so the loop asserts nothing and the preceding length>0 guard fails. Driver's pin independently proves fbMajorApplied===false on all 60 hits (rangeApplied not re-asserted — see rationale).

Bb '35.16%-per-stack ticks exist AND no 351.6 pre-multiplied instance' — GENUINE DIVERGENCE, documented (⚑4): driver ships one 351.6%/s instance (all 10 stacks applied per cast). S2b independently derived the same 10-stack opening from 'stacks up to 10 times' + 'the same targets' + the 10 sequential hits on a lone boss, so the driver's reading is cross-family corroborated and the blind's single-stack model is a 10× under-credit it flagged as unresolved.
Bb 'each DoT instance lasts 10s at 1s intervals' — RECON_ERROR: nearPct + sustained-selector bugs; the shipped dot is durationSec 10 / intervalSec 1 by inspection.
Bb 'removing the burst DoT lowers only sakura' — RECON_ERROR: same `ov.burst?.blocks` no-op patch as above.

skill2.driverSaid: passive/self buff, stat attackDamagePct, value 7.82 always-on = 15.64 × 90/180 (six 15s windows on the datamined 30s CD), ⚑3-flagged with the coupling to ⚑2 spelled out
skill2.blindSaid: S2b: attackDamagePct (NOT atkPct), self-only, 15s per CD, CD is ⚑-unknown. S6: attackDamagePct 15.64 durationSec 15 on interval:15 — same bucket, CD assumed = duration because the datamine was absent from its packet (explicitly flagged + recipe'd).
skill2.formulaCheck: Bucket is correct and is the trap both blinds named: 'Attack Damage ▲' → attackDamagePct (Damage-Up bucket), never atkPct — driver got it right. The magnitude follows the SSOT engine rule verbatim: a passive-trigger buff cannot carry a wall-clock duration (sim.ts alwaysOn), so a duration buff re-cast on a cooldown MUST be encoded as its time-average duty cycle. With the owner-confirmed skillCooldownsSec.skill2 = 30 → 15s/30s = 50% → 7.82. The blind's 15.64 assumes 100% uptime from a CD it did not have.
skill2.explanation: Applied once at frame 0 to targetIdx===SBIS with expiresFrame null (engine passive), and load-bearing: her normal-attack total sits strictly between the naive-15.64 and single-window-1.30 counterfactuals. Bucket identity is discriminated because the selector filters on stat==='attackDamagePct' and then asserts a non-empty [7.82] set — an atkPct encoding yields [] and goes RED. Residual (documented, not a gotcha): the time-average smears a bursty buff uniformly, so her burst volleys are credited ~50% Dancing Flower regardless of whether a real window was live at that cast — an engine limitation, second-order here since her casts straddle the windows either way.

skill2.driverSaid: dot atkPct 256, durationSec 15, intervalSec 1, flavor sustained, target enemy — passive block at t=0 plus an interval:30 block for the five re-casts = 6 windows / 90 ticks
skill2.blindSaid: S6 emitted a byte-identical dot effect (256 / 15 / 1 / sustained / enemy); only the cadence differs (interval 15 vs 30), which S6 flagged as its single largest unmeasured lever and recipe'd to the exact datamine field the driver holds. S2b: FAITHFUL, must not self-overlap.
skill2.formulaCheck: Sustained DoT routing is correct per the SSOT: ticks reference current buffs, take no core and no range, tick-crit default ON, FB by timing. Critically, S2b's taxonomy-#5 trap (per-fire 15s instances overlapping under a sub-15s CD and double-ticking a status the game maintains as one refreshed window) is NOT reachable here: durationSec 15 < interval 30, so windows abut with a 15s silent gap and concurrent instances never exceed 1 — the blind's own 15s cadence would have been the riskier encoding.
skill2.explanation: 90 ticks across six distinct 30s bands, all atkPct 256, all in the skill bucket, 15 per band; the drop-the-re-cast counterfactual collapses to exactly 15. Fires at the prose-implied cadence and is discriminated in both directions (no force-cast → 0 early ticks; no re-cast → 15 total).

burst.driverSaid: ten discrete flatDamage effects at atkPct 457.14, flavor sequential, in one burstCast block (kept as 10 instances so skill-gauge fires per hit and popups match); explicitly the fix for the materialized-freeze ×10 loss (same misparse class as crown)
burst.blindSaid: S6 emitted the identical ten-instance 457.14 sequential burstCast block. S2b: FAITHFUL, burstCast-keyed not fullBurstEnter (helm is co-B3 in the default fixture, so that divergence is LIVE), FB-exempt, 10 hits per cast.
burst.formulaCheck: Trigger identity is the high-risk call and the driver got it right: burstCast, so the volley fires only on HER casts, not on helm's — with helm co-B3 a fullBurstEnter encoding would roughly double the volleys. Per the measured FB-timing rule, damage dealt BY a burst skill AT its cast lands before the Full Burst window opens, so fbMajorApplied must be false — verified on all 60 hits.
burst.explanation: 60 hits over 6 sakura burstCasts, all atkPct 457.14, all in the burst bucket; the single-hit misparse counterfactual lands exactly 1/10 the hits. Three-way convergence on both the ten-instance shape and the FB exemption.

burst.driverSaid: one dot atkPct 351.6, durationSec 10, intervalSec 1, flavor sustained per burstCast — all 10 stacks applied at cast because the 10 sequential hits all land on the lone boss; ⚑4-flagged with a distinguishing recipe (flat ~351.6-scale ticks from the first second = hit-applied; growing ticks = ramp)
burst.blindSaid: S2b independently derived the SAME full-10-stack opening (≈351.6%/s for 10s, ⚑-flagged as a derivation from the volley targeting). S6 diverged low — one un-stacked 35.16 instance, calling the cap 'unreachable in practice' — a 10× under-credit it did not reconcile against 'the same targets' + 10 sequential hits.
burst.formulaCheck: The prose supplies both halves: 'Affects the same targets' ties the DoT to the volley's 10 sequential hits, and 'stacks up to 10 times' names the cap those hits reach on a single boss. The consolidation into one 351.6 instance instead of ten 35.16 instances is damage-identical (sustained bucket, linear) and nothing in this kit or the engine reads a stack COUNT, so the collapse costs no observable. Ticks correctly take FB by timing (no noFb on the dot) while the volley does not — the split S2b flagged as a misread risk is handled correctly.
burst.explanation: Ticks present at a single magnitude 351.6 in the burst bucket, flat from tick 1, with the single-stack counterfactual ticking at 35.16 — discriminated. Cross-family: the driver's reading is corroborated by S2b (fable) against S6's (opus) under-credit, i.e. the 2-of-3 majority is on the driver's side and the low reading is the outlier. ⚑ retained because instant-full-stacks is a derivation from targeting, not literal text — the recipe is recorded.

verdictRationale: Zero REAL-GOTCHAs survive. The S5 blind test run is RED, but the RED is not a faithfulness signal: three of its ten failures trace to two selector bugs (`nearPct` reads `ev.mult`, which is the multiplier-decomposition OBJECT rather than a number, so it returns false for EVERY event; and `sustained` filters on a `bucket==='sustained'`/`flavor` pair that damage events do not carry) and a third to counterfactual patches that mutate `ov.skill2?.blocks`/`ov.burst?.blocks` when the override file is slot-keyed — verifiable directly against §7b, where `override.skill2` IS the block array and no `.blocks` sub-array exists, making both 'load-bearing' patches provable no-ops. Eight of the ten failures are fully explained by those bugs and are RECON_ERROR. The remaining two are genuine, documented encoding divergences, and both resolve in the driver's favour: (1) Dancing Flower 7.82 vs the blind's 15.64 — the blind's own S6 caveat states it lacked skillCooldownsSec and recipes reading exactly the field the driver holds (skill2 CD = 30, owner-confirmed 2026-07-20); given that CD, the SSOT's passive-buff rule mandates the 50%-duty time-average 15.64 × 90/180 = 7.82, and the blind's 15.64 would over-credit 2×; (2) the burst DoT at 351.6%/s vs 35.16%/s — here the cross-family split favours the driver, since S2b (fable) independently derived the same full-10-stack opening from 'the same targets' + 'attacks sequentially 10 times' on a lone boss, and S6's single-stack model under-credits 10× while itself conceding the cap question was unresolved. On everything the blinds could derive from prose alone the convergence is structural and near-byte-identical: the 256/15/1/sustained enemy dot, the ten-instance 457.14 sequential burstCast volley, attackDamagePct (not atkPct) for Dancing Flower, burstCast keying rather than fullBurstEnter (live in this fixture because helm is co-B3), FB-exemption on the volley with FB-by-timing on the rider ticks, no core and no range anywhere, and all three part-destroy S1 lines as unmodeled-verbatim GAPs — the last confirmed by negative inertness assertions that PASSED in the blind's own file (no 5.1% sustainedDamagePct buff, no ~25s extension artifact). Every FAITHFUL block also demonstrably fires at the prose cadence rather than merely existing (90 petals ticks in six 30s bands, 15 per band; 60 volley hits over 6 casts; the buff applied at frame 0), and each load-bearing line has a named nearest-wrong counterfactual that goes RED, including the atkPct-vs-attackDamagePct bucket trap (the stat-filtered selector yields an empty set and fails under an atkPct encoding). Faithfulness 8/8 = 1.0; GO. Same-model residual for owner spot-check, in priority order: (a) the volley's `rangeApplied` is the one assertion nobody actually executed — the blind's check was voided by its nearPct bug and the driver's pin does not re-assert it, and S6 defensively wrote `noRange: true` where the driver relies on an engine default; a 5-minute event-field check closes it (the SSOT says burst damage takes no range bucket, so a mismatch would be an engine bug, not an encoding one). (b) Same shape for `crit` on the flatDamage effects — S6 wrote `crit: true` explicitly, the driver omits it; confirm the schema default is crit-eligible for burst-bucket flatDamage. (c) The Dancing Flower time-average smears a 50%-duty buff uniformly across a bursty damage profile; if a future engine gains duration-carrying passives, re-window it rather than re-tune the 7.82. (d) ⚑4 remains genuinely unmeasured — the instant-full-10-stacks reading is a derivation from targeting, not literal prose; the recorded recipe (read sustained tick popups immediately after her burst: flat ~351.6%-scale from the first second = hit-applied, growing = ramp) is the cheapest way to retire it, and it is worth ~0.55× on that block if the ramp reading wins.
